name: Word Clock
description: Tell the time in words, QLOCKTWO style, in German, English, Spanish or French. Adapts to Flagship and Note.
author: Oliver Rummeyer

language.title: Language
language.description: Language the time is spelled out in.

timezone.title: Timezone
timezone.description: IANA timezone name (e.g. Europe/Berlin). Leave empty to follow the FiestaBoard-wide timezone.

show_prefix.title: Show "ES IST" / "IT IS" / "SON LAS" / "IL EST"
show_prefix.description: Dropped automatically if the phrase would not fit the board.

german_style.title: German dialect
german_style.description: Standard uses VIERTEL NACH / VIERTEL VOR. Regional (East German, Franconian, Saxon) uses VIERTEL ZEHN / DREIVIERTEL ZEHN and counts :20 and :40 from HALB. Only applies to German.

umlauts.title: Umlauts
umlauts.description: The board has no umlaut tiles. Expand writes FUENF and ZWOELF, Strip writes FUNF and ZWOLF. Only German words carry umlauts; the other languages are unaffected.

rounding.title: Rounding
rounding.description: Down matches a physical word clock: the phrase changes on every full five minutes. Nearest rounds to the closest five-minute step.

show_minute_dots.title: Show minute dots
show_minute_dots.description: Adds up to four colored tiles in the bottom right for the minutes the words cannot express, like the corner dots on a QLOCKTWO. Requires Down rounding to be meaningful; skipped when the bottom row is full.

phrase.description: Full spelled-out time including the prefix

phrase_short.description: Spelled-out time without the ES IST / IT IS prefix

prefix.description: The opener, empty when disabled. Spanish agrees it with the hour (ES LA / SON LAS).

block.description: The whole laid-out board as one value, rows separated by newlines. Put this on the first template line to fill the board with the centered phrase. Length is geometry-dependent -- 2903 is the worst case, the largest note array (120x24) -- so it is far short of that on a Flagship or Note.

line1.description: Board row 1 of the laid-out phrase, padded to the board width. Width is geometry-dependent -- 120 is the worst case, the widest note array -- so this is far short of 120 characters on a Flagship or Note.
